Subject: Post-call: RAG eval - next steps

Thanks again for the time today -- great conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side: 

- Goal: Reduce hallucination and improve grounding for knowledge-base answers in the customer support workflow; target latency ~300ms p95 for single-turn assisted responses.
- What we heard: corpus ~3M docs (mostly short KB articles + 200k long policy PDFs), ingestion cadence nightly, strict grounding requirement for flagged answers.
- Early recommendations (high-level):
  * Retriever: dense embeddings + metadata filter for product/region.
  * Index: FAISS HNSW with sharding by product line.
  * Reranker: cross-encoder reranker for top-10 results to improve grounding precision.
  * Embedding model: text-embedding-redwood-2 (1536-d) or a comparable production embedding.

Attached: quick bench of our first-pass retrieval/grounding metrics (acme-rag-eval-benchmarks.csv) and a proposed prompt-set for evals (proposed-prompt-sets.md).

Proposed immediate next steps:
1) Dev-led tech sync (30m) to confirm retrieval settings & chunking strategy -- can you confirm Tues 4/20 10am PT?
2) We'll run a controlled reranker test (roberta-cross-encoder baseline) over your sample eval set and share detailed grounding metrics (precision@k, hallucination rate, MRR).
3) If results look good, schedule a short pilot (2 weeks) to validate latency/cost tradeoffs.

Please confirm the 4/20 slot or suggest alternatives.

-- Marissa

- The corpus size I quoted (~3M) is compressed docs; uncompressed token count is closer to 1.1B tokens. We can provide a 50k-sample eval set (questions + trusted-source labels) by Monday.

From: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
To: Sam Johnson <sam.johnson@acme.com>, Priya Menon <priya.menon@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-19T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: RAG eval - next steps (retriever & reranker config)

Hey team -- follow-up from the engineering side with a concrete config and tradeoffs. TL;DR: two-stage retrieval + lightweight reranker is the pragmatic starting point. Details: 

1) Retrieval stage (candidate generation)
- Embedding model: text-embedding-redwood-2 (1536-d) or OpenEmbed-v1 if you prefer parity; dimension determines index choice and memory.
- Index: FAISS HNSW for speed + approximate recall; for 3M docs compressed ~8-12GB per shard depending on quantization.
- Search params: ef_search=200, ef_construction=64 (tune as needed); candidate k=100.
- Chunking: 1,000 token sliding window with 200 token overlap for PDFs, KBs keep smaller chunks (~200-400 tokens) to preserve answer spans.
- Metadata filters: product_id and region tags applied at query time to reduce false positives.

2) Reranking stage (precision & grounding)
- Baseline: cross-encoder (roberta-large-msmarco or distilled variants) applied to top-10 from retriever.
- Cost/latency note: running full cross-attention on top-10 is typically acceptable at sub-second latency if you have GPU-backed nodes and batch small queries; reranker_top_k=10 is a good balance.
- Alternative: lightweight pointwise reranker (distil-bert) + thresholding to reduce cross-encoder calls only to ambiguous queries. This hybrid reduces cost by ~3x.

3) Scoring & grounding heuristics
- Score composition: final_score = alpha * normalized_retriever_score + beta * reranker_score + gamma * metadata_match (alpha/beta/gamma tuned on eval set).
- Grounding threshold: require at least one result with reranker_score >= 0.75 AND answer token overlap >= 0.6 with the retrieved span to mark "grounded".

4) Evaluation metrics we will run (these will be in the bench CSV):
- Grounding precision@k (percentage of answers flagged as grounded where source contains the ground-truth span)
- Hallucination rate (answers with no matching span in top-k)
- MRR, nDCG@10, Recall@k (k=10,100)
- Latency p95 for combined retrieval+rerank pipeline (target <300ms)
- Cost per 1k queries estimate (with GPU reranker vs hybrid)

5) Regression / monitoring checks to add to pilot:
- Periodic prompt-set evaluation: run daily signals on a small set of 500 queries to detect drift/regression in grounding precision.
- Quality alerting: trigger on >5% drop in grounding precision or >3% increase in hallucination rate week-over-week.

Next actions from engineering:
- We'll run two configurations on your sample eval set: (A) dense retriever + cross-encoder reranker (top-10) and (B) dense retriever + lightweight reranker + conditional cross-encoder.
- Expect initial results within 48-72 hours of the sample eval arriving.

Happy to go deeper on the quantization/throughput numbers on the tech sync.

-- Dev Patel
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
